title: Iridescent Coating Synthesis Lab
description: A virtual chemistry lab where the user synthesizes iridescent nacre coatings from an abalone shell specimen and applies them to a shoe prototype as a materials science experiment. The user must balance reagent concentrations, pH levels, and temperature while obeying conservation of total solute mass across reaction vessels, with full undo/redo support for each step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap with cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load IridescenceAbalone.glb as a specimen on the left lab bench and MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb as the coating target on the right bench. Use GLTFLoader; for the shoe, enumerate its material variants via KHR_materials_variants and display variant buttons. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,3) looking at origin, with OrbitControls limited to lab area. Lighting: one DirectionalLight (warm white), one HemisphereLight, and a PointLight near the abalone to highlight iridescence. Build an HTML overlay panel with: (1) three reagent sliders (CaCO3, Conchiolin, Aragonite) each 0-100, enforcing conservation law so their sum always equals 100 — adjusting one auto-reduces others proportionally; (2) a pH slider (1-14) and temperature slider (20-200°C); (3) an 'Extract' button that animates particles flowing from the abalone into a beaker (a simple translucent cylinder mesh); (4) a 'Synthesize' button that changes the beaker liquid color based on reagent ratios and pH; (5) a 'Coat' button that lerps the shoe's material properties (metalness, roughness, iridescence intensity, iridescence IOR) toward values derived from current reagent/pH/temp settings, with a particle stream animation from beaker to shoe; (6) a variant selector to switch the shoe variant before or after coating; (7) Undo and Redo buttons maintaining a history stack of all slider changes, extractions, syntheses, coatings, and variant switches (10-14 steps expected). Each coating application should visually accumulate on the shoe (increase iridescence intensity additively, clamp at 1.0). Display a lab notebook text area logging each action with timestamp. The beaker volume is conserved: extracting adds volume, coating consumes it — disable Coat when empty. Target 12 interaction steps for a full experiment cycle: set three reagents, adjust pH, adjust temp, extract, synthesize, select variant, coat, undo coating, redo coating, change variant, coat again, final extract.
